diagnostics.title: A2A per-task provenance chain failed verification on restore (tamper evidence)
diagnostics.summary: When the plane restored its task records after its instance opened, an in-flight task's per-task provenance chain did NOT verify: the host reported a break on that task's chain. This is distinct from a row that merely could not be read (BUSBAR-7024): the bytes were read and the chain does not add up, which is tamper evidence — the durable task state was altered out from under busbar, or its store is corrupt. The task is still held and served: a break is reported, never a deletion, because deleting on a break would let anyone able to write the store erase a caller's task. Emitted once per affected in-flight task on each restore.
diagnostics.action: Treat the durable A2A task store as compromised until explained: capture it for forensic review before it is overwritten, and restore it from a trusted backup once the cause is understood. The named task stays held; other tasks are unaffected.

diagnostics.title: A2A submission not accepted (the pool's members are not interchangeable)
diagnostics.summary: A submission targeted an agent pool whose members are not interchangeable under the seam's rules, so it was not accepted. A routine per-request routing refusal, benign and expected under the configured pool policy; surfaced at debug so a busy caller cannot spam the log.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. If submissions should route, configure the pool's members to be interchangeable (matching capabilities) so the seam can dispatch across them.

diagnostics.title: Outbound A2A credential could not be leased
diagnostics.summary: busbar could not lease the outbound credential needed to make a hop to the target agent, so the hop is refused. The egress-auth path that mints or fetches the credential for this agent failed. Usually an egress-auth wiring or credential-source problem.
diagnostics.action: Check the egress-auth configuration and credential source for the named agent (scopes, the credential plugin/store). Outbound hops resume once a credential can be leased.

diagnostics.title: Relayed A2A stream ended in a refusal
diagnostics.summary: A relayed streaming task ended in a refusal from the backend rather than a normal completion. The refusal is recorded against the task and the caller's poll will find it. Per-request and expected under normal backend policy, so surfaced at debug.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. A stream that ends in a refusal reflects the backend's own decision; the recorded refusal is what the caller reads.

diagnostics.title: Relayed A2A task outcome could not be recorded (durable store write failed)
diagnostics.summary: A relayed hop SUCCEEDED and the caller is owed its answer, but the resulting state transition could not be written to the durable task store. Reported, never fatal: a store that refused the transition is an operator problem, not a reason to discard completed, billed work. Warned once on the transition; subsequent failures hold at debug.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the durable task-store outage. The caller still receives the completed hop; only the durable outcome record failed and resumes once the store accepts writes.

diagnostics.title: Relayed A2A task submission failed
diagnostics.summary: A relayed task submission was refused by the backend. The refusal is recorded against the task and returned to the caller; busbar did not accept work it could not place. Per-request and expected under normal backend policy or load, so surfaced at debug.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. A submission the backend refuses reflects the backend's own decision or capacity; the caller reads the recorded refusal and may re-submit.

diagnostics.title: Failed A2A task could not be recorded as failed (durable store write failed)
diagnostics.summary: A task reached the terminal `failed` state but that transition could not be written to the durable task store, so a durable row may still claim the work is in flight. The caller is answered and any registered callback is fired; the durable record is what failed. Typically a store outage. Warned once on the transition; then held at debug.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the durable task-store outage. The caller was told of the failure; the durable `failed` record resumes once the store accepts writes.

diagnostics.title: Persisted A2A task rows could not be read back (not resumable)
diagnostics.summary: When the plane restored its task records after its instance opened, some persisted A2A task rows could not be read back and are therefore NOT resumable — most likely written by a different busbar version. Reported separately from the restored count and at warn, because folding an unreadable in-flight task into the restored total is how a task that silently ceased to exist across a deploy stays invisible.
diagnostics.action: Expected once after a version change; the counted rows cannot be resumed by this binary. If it recurs without a version change, inspect the durable task store for corruption. Callers of the affected tasks may re-submit.

diagnostics.title: Durable A2A task state could not be read on restore (nothing counted or chain-checked)
diagnostics.summary: When the plane restored its task records after its instance opened, the durable A2A task records could not be listed at all, so nothing was counted and no in-flight task's provenance chain was checked. Serving does not wait on the restore: each task is still read from its own record when a request names it, and a request the store cannot answer is refused. Typically a durable-store outage.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the durable task store outage. Once it answers, requests read their tasks again; restart to have the restore count the tasks and check their chains.

diagnostics.title: A2A card or approval record split across host records was not read back whole
diagnostics.summary: When the plane warmed its agent cards after its instance opened, a card or card approval that was written split across several host records (it was larger than the host's record ceiling) could not be reassembled: a part is missing, or the parts do not verify against the digest the record's head states. The record is not read, so that agent is looked at afresh, as if no such record were held; the record is written again on the agent's next connect or approve. Emitted once per affected record on each warm.
diagnostics.action: Check the durable record store for lost or altered records (an interrupted write, a store restored from an older backup, or a write from outside busbar), and the named agent's card and approval state.

diagnostics.title: A2A card or approval part records that no whole record names were found
diagnostics.summary: When the plane warmed its agent cards after its instance opened, it found part records of a split card or card approval that no whole record names: left by a write that was interrupted or superseded. They are never read; each is tombstoned on its agent's next connect or approve. Emitted once per kind on each warm that finds any; the `parts` field carries how many.
diagnostics.action: None; self-heals. The stray parts are tombstoned when their agent's record is next written. If the count grows across restarts, check the durable record store for failing writes.

diagnostics.title: A2A far-end task id longer than the plane holds was not recorded
diagnostics.summary: An agent answered a task with its own task id, and that id is longer than the plane holds (1024 bytes): the far end's ids are untrusted input, and the map that translates them is bounded in bytes as it is in entries. The id is not recorded, so the task keeps busbar's own id and a later request naming the task reaches the agent under busbar's id, which the agent may not know. The `task` field carries busbar's task id and `bytes` the length the agent named.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the named agent: it issues task ids far longer than any A2A agent needs. Follow-up requests on the affected tasks may be answered 'task not found' by the agent until it issues ids of an ordinary length.

diagnostics.title: A2A agent endpoint refused before the hop
diagnostics.summary: Before a relayed request was sent, the agent's registered url was refused by the relay's guard: its scheme is plaintext on a registration without `allow_private`, or the host's destination judgement refused the host or an address it resolves to. The caller is answered the hop's fixed refusal words; this diagnostic carries the guard's own sentence, naming the url and why, which the caller is never shown. Emitted on each refused hop.
diagnostics.action: Correct the named agent's registration: use an https:// url, or set `allow_private: true` if the endpoint is a loopback or private one the operator means to reach; for a refused address, check the agent's DNS and the deployment's destination policy.

diagnostics.title: A2A agent card sighting not recorded on the kernel's trust book
diagnostics.summary: The plane looked at an agent's card (on connect, approve, or the re-verification before a relayed call) and reported what it saw to the kernel's trust book, and the host failed that report. The kernel was never told the card's fingerprint, so its verdict still answers for the card it last saw: the look fails closed, no card is held from it, and the agent is not served on it (connect and approve report the failure). Emitted once per failed report; the `agent` field names the agent.
diagnostics.action: Check the host's trust service and its durable store: a trust book that cannot record sightings leaves every re-verified agent refused until it can. The agent is looked at again on its next call or verb.

diagnostics.title: A2A task push config could not be read; a notification was not sent
diagnostics.summary: A relayed task moved, and the push config its caller registered for it could not be read from the durable record store. A failed read is not taken as 'no config': no notification is queued to a destination guessed without it, and the credential a registered receiver is owed is kept for the notifications still waiting. The notification this move owed is not sent. The `task` field names busbar's task id.
diagnostics.action: Check the durable record store's health. The caller can read the task's state with tasks/get; later moves of the task are notified once the store reads again.

diagnostics.title: A2A stored card or approval record could not be read
diagnostics.summary: When the plane warmed its agent cards after its instance opened, a stored card or card-approval record read back whole but is not the JSON the plane wrote (a card that is not a JSON document, an approval that is not a map of skill digests). The record is not used: the agent holds no card from it, so its calls are refused until it is looked at again, and its approved skills are not restored for the trust view. Emitted once per affected record on each warm; the `kind` and `agent` fields name it.
diagnostics.action: Run connect (and approve, if the agent was approved) for the named agent: that writes the record again. Check the durable record store for writes from outside busbar or a restore from an incompatible backup.

diagnostics.title: A relayed SSE frame was not valid UTF-8 and was dropped
diagnostics.summary: The shared SSE frame reader (the JSON-RPC plane relays) assembled a complete event whose bytes are not valid UTF-8. The event-stream format is UTF-8 BY DEFINITION, so this is a malformed backend; the frame is DROPPED rather than lossily transcoded, which would hand the client a corrupted payload. The stream itself continues, so a client sees a missing event, not a failure. The `bytes` field carries the size of the frame that was dropped.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the named backend agent: its event stream is emitting non-UTF-8 bytes, which no conforming event-stream consumer can read. Until it is fixed the affected events are lost; busbar relays every well-formed event around them.
